instructions: Each template provides a complete content structure. Variables in {brackets} are auto-filled from post data. Writers fill in the [...] placeholders.

templates.name: How-To Tutorial

structure.guidance: Open with the problem or pain point the reader is experiencing. State what they will be able to do by the end. Include focus keyword in first 100 words. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: What You Need Before You Start
structure.guidance: List prerequisites, tools, or knowledge needed. Use a bullet list. Keep it short — 3-5 items max. 50-100 words.

structure.heading: Step 1: [First Major Action]
structure.guidance: Start with the easiest or most foundational step. Include a screenshot or image. Explain WHY this step matters, not just how to do it. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Step 2: [Second Major Action]
structure.guidance: Continue the logical sequence. Add a pro tip box here. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Step 3: [Third Major Action]
structure.guidance: Mid-point of the process. This is often the most complex step — break it into substeps using H3. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Step 5: [Fifth Major Action]
structure.guidance: The final or near-final step. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Common Mistakes to Avoid
structure.guidance: List 3-5 mistakes people make with this process. Each with a brief explanation. Highly shareable section. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: Answer 4-5 questions from Google's People Also Ask for this topic. 40-60 words per answer. Apply FAQPage schema.

structure.heading: Final Thoughts
structure.guidance: Summarize key steps in 2-3 sentences. End with an action-oriented question to encourage comments. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Focus keyword must appear in: title, intro, at least one H2, conclusion. Include year in title for freshness. Add numbered list of steps near top for featured snippet potential.

templates.name: Listicle / Roundup

structure.guidance: State the list topic and why it matters. Preview the selection criteria (why these specific items made the list). 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Quick Summary Table
structure.guidance: Add a comparison table showing all items with 3-4 key attributes. Great for featured snippets and skimmers.

structure.heading: 1. [Item Name] — [One-Line Description]
structure.guidance: For each list item: what it is, key features/benefits, who it's best for, any downsides, and a verdict. 150-250 words per item.

structure.note: Repeat the item structure for each entry in the list. Aim for 7-15 items total for comprehensive coverage.

structure.heading: How We Selected These [Items]
structure.guidance: Explain your evaluation criteria. Builds credibility and E-E-A-T. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 4-5 FAQs about the list topic. Apply FAQPage schema.

structure.heading: Which [Item] Is Right for You?
structure.guidance: Give a decision framework based on reader type/needs. Recommend 1-2 top picks for different scenarios. 100-150 words.

templates.seo_notes: Use exact number in title (e.g., '11 Best...', not 'Top'). Update annually. Link to individual reviews for each item where they exist.

templates.name: Ultimate Pillar Guide

structure.guidance: Define the topic, explain why it matters in {year}, and preview exactly what the guide covers. Include a Table of Contents with anchor links. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: What Is {keyword}?
structure.guidance: Clear definition. Include history/context. Explain why it matters now more than ever. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: How {keyword} Works
structure.guidance: The mechanics. Use diagrams or flowcharts if possible. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: Chapter 1: [Foundational Concept]
structure.guidance: First major subtopic. Comprehensive coverage with examples. 400-600 words.

structure.heading: Chapter 2: [Core Strategy]
structure.guidance: Second major subtopic. 400-600 words.

structure.heading: Chapter 3: [Advanced Tactics]
structure.guidance: Third major subtopic. 400-600 words.

structure.heading: Chapter 4: [Tools and Resources]
structure.guidance: Recommended tools, software, or resources. Can be a listicle within the guide. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: Chapter 5: [Common Mistakes]
structure.guidance: What not to do. Very shareable section. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: Chapter 6: [Real-World Examples]
structure.guidance: Case studies or examples showing the concepts in action. 300-500 words.

structure.heading: {keyword} Checklist
structure.guidance: Actionable summary checklist readers can bookmark. Highly shareable. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 6-8 FAQs covering the full breadth of the topic. Apply FAQPage schema.

structure.heading: Next Steps
structure.guidance: What to do first after reading. Link to related posts for further reading. 150-200 words.

templates.seo_notes: This is a pillar page — it should link out to all cluster content on subtopics. Include Table of Contents. Target broad head keywords (1-2 words). Aim for the featured snippet on 'what is X' queries.

templates.name: Product / Tool Review

structure.guidance: Who you are, how long you've used the product, and your overall verdict upfront (don't bury the lead). 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Quick Verdict
structure.guidance: Score out of 10, pros list (5 items), cons list (3 items), best for, not for. Use a styled box. Skimmers read this first.

structure.heading: What Is {product}?
structure.guidance: Brief overview — what it does, who makes it, pricing tiers. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Key Features
structure.guidance: Go through 5-8 main features in depth. For each: describe it, show a screenshot, give your honest experience. 600-900 words.

structure.heading: Pricing and Plans
structure.guidance: Break down all pricing tiers clearly. Include a comparison table. Mention free trial or money-back guarantee. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: How It Compares to Alternatives
structure.guidance: Compare briefly to 2-3 top competitors. Use a table. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Who Should Use {product}?
structure.guidance: Be specific — give 3 audience types it's perfect for and 2 it's not for. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5-6 FAQs about the product. Apply FAQPage schema.

structure.heading: Final Verdict
structure.guidance: Restate your recommendation. Include a CTA to try the product. Mention your overall score. 100-150 words.

templates.seo_notes: Add Review schema with your rating. Include the product name + 'review' + year in title. Link to the official product page. Include your real screenshots — not stock photos.

templates.name: Comparison Post (A vs B)

structure.guidance: State the comparison, why it matters, and who this guide is for. Give a quick bottom line up front. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Quick Comparison Table
structure.guidance: Side-by-side table with 8-10 key criteria. Use checkmarks and X marks. This is your featured snippet target.

structure.heading: {Option A} Overview
structure.guidance: What it is, who makes it, main strengths, main weaknesses, pricing. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: {Option B} Overview
structure.guidance: Same structure as Option A. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Feature-by-Feature Comparison
structure.guidance: Go through 6-8 key feature categories and compare both options for each. Use H3 for each category. 600-800 words.

structure.heading: Pricing Comparison
structure.guidance: Detailed pricing breakdown for both. Include total cost of ownership. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: When to Choose {Option A}
structure.guidance: 3-4 specific scenarios where Option A clearly wins. Be specific about the type of user. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: When to Choose {Option B}
structure.guidance: 3-4 specific scenarios where Option B wins. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5 FAQs about the comparison. Apply FAQPage schema.

structure.heading: Our Recommendation
structure.guidance: Give a clear winner for 2-3 specific audience types. Don't sit on the fence — readers want a decision. 100-150 words.

templates.seo_notes: Target '[Option A] vs [Option B]' exact keyword. Include both product names in URL. Add comparison table near top for featured snippet. Update pricing quarterly.

templates.name: Case Study

structure.guidance: State the result upfront (e.g., '312% traffic increase in 6 months'). Brief context on who was involved. Establish credibility. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: The Challenge
structure.guidance: What problem were you trying to solve? What was the starting state? Include baseline metrics. 200-250 words.

structure.heading: Our Strategy
structure.guidance: What approach did you take? Why did you choose this over alternatives? Be specific — this is your expertise showcase. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: Implementation: What We Did Step by Step
structure.guidance: The exact actions taken in chronological order. Include timelines. The more specific, the more trustworthy. 400-600 words.

structure.heading: The Results
structure.guidance: Show the data. Use charts, screenshots, or tables. Include before/after comparisons. Be specific with numbers. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Key Takeaways
structure.guidance: 3-5 lessons learned that apply broadly to readers. This is what makes the case study universally valuable. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: What We Would Do Differently
structure.guidance: Honest reflection on mistakes or missed opportunities. Builds trust enormously. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Can You Replicate These Results?
structure.guidance: Set realistic expectations. Explain what factors contributed most to success. CTA to try the approach. 100-150 words.

templates.seo_notes: Include specific metrics in title and meta description. Use before/after data as pull quotes. Highly linkable — pitch to industry publications after publishing.

templates.name: Beginner's Guide

structure.guidance: Immediately reassure the reader this is designed for beginners. Define what they'll know by the end. Validate their starting point — no shame in being new. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: What Is {keyword}? (And Why Does It Matter?)
structure.guidance: Plain English definition. Real-world analogy to explain the concept. Why it matters in {year}. 200-250 words.

structure.heading: Key Terms You Need to Know
structure.guidance: A mini glossary of 6-10 essential terms. Readers will bookmark this. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: How {keyword} Works (Simply Explained)
structure.guidance: The mechanism, explained simply. Use an analogy. No jargon. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Getting Started: Your First Steps
structure.guidance: The 3-5 actions a complete beginner should take first. Very specific and actionable. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: Common Beginner Mistakes
structure.guidance: 5 mistakes new people make. Validate that they're common — makes readers feel less alone. 200-250 words.

structure.heading: Recommended Tools for Beginners
structure.guidance: 3-5 beginner-friendly tools. Focus on free or cheap options. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: What to Learn Next
structure.guidance: A clear learning path with links to intermediate resources. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5 questions beginners always ask. Apply FAQPage schema.
Encouragement. Recap the key first steps. Ask what their biggest challenge is in the comments. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Use 'beginners', 'for beginners', 'getting started' in title and headings. Avoid jargon in the entire piece. Short sentences, simple words throughout.

templates.name: SEO-Optimized Blog Post

structure.guidance: Hook with a surprising stat, bold claim, or relatable problem. State what the post covers. Include focus keyword. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: [Main Point or Concept 1]
structure.guidance: First major point. Start with the most important or surprising insight. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: [Main Point or Concept 2]
structure.guidance: Second point that builds on the first. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: [Main Point or Concept 3]
structure.guidance: Third point. Include a real example or data point here. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: [Actionable Strategy or Tactic]
structure.guidance: What should the reader actually DO with this information? The practical application section. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 3-4 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.
Summarize key points. End with a question to drive comments. Optional CTA to related content. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Keyword in title (front-loaded), URL, meta, H1, first paragraph, one H2, conclusion. Target one primary keyword. Use LSI keywords throughout.

templates.name: What Is / Definition Post

structure.guidance: Give the direct answer immediately in the first paragraph — Google often pulls this for featured snippets. 50-100 words.

structure.heading: What Is {keyword}? (Full Explanation)
structure.guidance: Expanded definition with context and examples. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: How {keyword} Works
structure.guidance: The mechanism or process explained simply. 200-250 words.

structure.heading: Types of {keyword}
structure.guidance: If applicable — categorize the concept into 3-5 types with brief explanations. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Why {keyword} Matters
structure.guidance: Real-world importance and consequences of understanding or ignoring it. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: {keyword} Examples
structure.guidance: 3-5 real-world examples. Concrete examples are the most shared parts of definition posts. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema. Target PAA questions from Google.
One-paragraph summary. Link to related deeper-dive posts. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Put the concise definition in the first paragraph for featured snippet targeting. Use 'What is X' or 'X definition' as keyword. Include 40-50 word summary at top.

templates.name: Checklist Post

structure.guidance: Why this checklist exists and who it's for. How to use it. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: Quick Checklist (Print-Friendly)
structure.guidance: A condensed version of the full checklist — just the action items without explanation. Users can print or screenshot this. Highly shareable.

structure.heading: Section 1: [Category of Checklist Items]
structure.guidance: 5-8 checklist items with brief explanations (2-3 sentences each). 200-350 words.

structure.heading: Section 2: [Second Category]
structure.guidance: 5-8 more checklist items. 200-350 words.

structure.heading: Section 3: [Third Category]
structure.guidance: 5-8 more checklist items. 200-350 words.

structure.heading: Common Questions About This Checklist
structure.guidance: 3-4 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.

structure.heading: How to Use This Checklist
structure.guidance: Recommended workflow for working through the checklist. Frequency recommendation. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Include the word 'checklist' in title, URL, and H1. Structure is perfect for featured snippets. Add downloadable PDF version as a lead magnet.

templates.name: Troubleshooting / Fix Guide

structure.guidance: Validate the reader's frustration immediately. State the problem clearly. Brief overview of solutions covered. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: Why This Problem Happens
structure.guidance: Explain the root causes. Understanding why helps readers prevent recurrence. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Quick Fixes to Try First
structure.guidance: 3-4 simple solutions that solve the problem 80% of the time. Try these before the advanced fixes. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Fix 1: [Specific Solution]
structure.guidance: Step-by-step fix. Include screenshots. State when this fix applies. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Fix 2: [Specific Solution]
structure.guidance: Step-by-step fix. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Fix 3: [Specific Solution]
structure.guidance: Step-by-step fix. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: When to Ask for Help
structure.guidance: Signs the problem is beyond a DIY fix and needs professional attention. Links to support resources. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: How to Prevent This Problem
structure.guidance: Proactive steps to ensure this doesn't happen again. Very valuable section. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 4-5 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.

templates.seo_notes: Target error message text as keywords — people search the exact error. Title format: '[Error/Problem]: How to Fix It'. High commercial intent.

templates.name: Expert Roundup

structure.guidance: Introduce the question you asked experts. Why this question matters now. Brief bio of the types of experts included. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Key Themes from the Experts
structure.guidance: Summary of the most common or interesting patterns in the responses. 200-300 words. Great for skimmers.

structure.heading: [Expert Name], [Title] at [Company]
structure.guidance: For each expert: their headshot, title, company, and their full response. 100-300 words per expert. Aim for 15-25 experts.

structure.note: Repeat expert entry structure for all experts

structure.heading: Our Takeaway
structure.guidance: Your own synthesis of the expert advice. What's the actionable conclusion? 150-200 words.

templates.seo_notes: Extremely linkable — email each expert after publishing asking them to share. Each expert's mention = potential backlink. Include expert names in meta description.

templates.name: Tools Roundup

structure.guidance: Why these tools, how they were selected, brief overview of categories covered. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Quick Comparison Table
structure.guidance: Table showing all tools with: price, best for, free plan availability, rating. Skimmers read this first.

structure.heading: 1. {Tool Name} — Best for [Use Case]
structure.guidance: For each tool: what it does, standout features, pricing, pros, cons, best for. 200-350 words per tool.

structure.note: Repeat for all tools. Group into categories if covering many tools.

structure.heading: How to Choose the Right Tool
structure.guidance: Decision framework based on team size, budget, and use case. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5 FAQs about the tool category. Apply FAQPage schema.

structure.heading: Our Top Picks
structure.guidance: Final recommendations for different reader types. 100-150 words.

templates.seo_notes: Target 'best [tool type] tools' keyword. Update annually. Include affiliate links where applicable — clearly disclosed. High commercial intent.

templates.name: Statistics Roundup

structure.guidance: Why these stats matter. How and when data was collected. State the key headline stat immediately. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Key {keyword} Statistics (Quick Summary)
structure.guidance: 5-7 most impressive stats as highlighted callouts. Highly shareable and screenshot-worthy.

structure.heading: {Category 1} Statistics
structure.guidance: Group stats by theme. For each stat: the number, the source, and a brief interpretation. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: {Category 2} Statistics
structure.guidance: Second category of stats. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: {Category 3} Statistics
structure.guidance: Third category. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: What These Statistics Mean for You
structure.guidance: Practical takeaways from the data. This is what makes it actionable. 200-300 words.
When you'll next update this post. Invite readers to submit missing stats. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Extremely linkable — people link to stats posts constantly. Update annually. Title: '{Number} {Topic} Statistics You Need to Know in {Year}'. Each stat should link to its primary source.

templates.name: News / Trend Post

structure.guidance: The news or trend, stated clearly upfront. What happened and why it matters. Lead with the most important information (inverted pyramid). 100-150 words.

structure.heading: What Changed (And Why)
structure.guidance: Full context of the change or trend. Background for readers who missed earlier coverage. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: What This Means for {audience}
structure.guidance: Direct implications for the reader. Be specific. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: What You Should Do Now
structure.guidance: 3-5 specific action items the reader should take in response. 150-250 words.
Invite discussion. What does the reader think? Link to related posts. 50-75 words.

templates.seo_notes: Publish FAST — news SEO is time-sensitive. Include the date/year in the URL for evergreen tracking. Submit URL to Google Search Console for faster indexing.

templates.name: WooCommerce Product Page

structure.guidance: Lead with the product's #1 benefit — not features. Who is this for and what problem does it solve? First sentence should be a benefit statement. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: What's Included
structure.guidance: Everything in the box or package. Use a bullet list. Be specific about dimensions, materials, quantities. 50-100 words.

structure.heading: Key Features and Benefits
structure.guidance: 5-7 features, each written as a benefit (what it does FOR the customer). Avoid spec sheets — translate specs into outcomes. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Who This Is For
structure.guidance: 2-3 specific customer types. Also mention who it's NOT for — builds trust. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 4-5 product-specific FAQs. Reduces pre-sale anxiety and returns. Apply FAQPage schema.

templates.seo_notes: Apply full Product schema with price, availability, and aggregate rating. Target '[product name]' and '[product category] [use case]' keywords. Unique description — never copy manufacturer text.

templates.name: Local Business Landing Page

structure.guidance: Service + location in the first sentence. Primary benefit. Phone number or CTA visible above fold. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: {Service} in {Location} — What We Offer
structure.guidance: Clear list of services. Use bullets. Include service areas. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Why Choose Us for {Service} in {Location}
structure.guidance: 3-5 differentiators. Years in business, certifications, guarantees, response time. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Our Recent Work in {Location}
structure.guidance: 2-3 brief case studies or project descriptions with outcomes. Photos if possible. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: What Our {Location} Customers Say
structure.guidance: 3-5 customer testimonials. Include full name and neighborhood if possible. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 4-5 FAQs specific to local service. Apply FAQPage schema.

structure.heading: Get a Free Quote Today
structure.guidance: Clear CTA. Phone number, email, or form. Business hours. Address with embedded map. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Apply LocalBusiness schema with full NAP (Name, Address, Phone). Target '[service] [city]' keyword. Include Google Maps embed. NAP must match Google Business Profile exactly.

templates.name: Glossary / Dictionary Post

structure.guidance: Why this glossary was created, who it's for, and how to use it. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: A
structure.guidance: All terms starting with A. Each term: bold the term, 1-2 sentence plain English definition, optional example. 100-200 words per letter.

structure.note: Continue A-Z. Focus on letters with the most industry terms. Skip letters with no relevant terms.

structure.guidance: Invite readers to submit missing terms. 50 words.

templates.seo_notes: Extremely linkable — writers link to glossaries constantly. Add anchor links for each letter. Target '[industry] glossary' and '[industry] terminology' keywords. Add DefinedTerm schema for each entry.

templates.name: Interview Post

structure.guidance: Who the interviewee is, why they're worth listening to, and the key topic of conversation. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: About {Interviewee Name}
structure.guidance: Brief bio — credentials, experience, notable achievements. Link to their website/social. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: The Interview
structure.guidance: Q&A format. Bold each question. Keep questions conversational but insightful. 1500-2500 words total across all Q&As.

structure.heading: Key Takeaways
structure.guidance: Top 3-5 insights from the interview in bullet format. Excellent for skimmers. 100-150 words.
Thank the interviewee. Link to their resources. Ask readers what they thought. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: The interviewee's name is a long-tail keyword. Ask interviewee to share on social — this drives initial traffic. Include interview date in the post.

templates.name: Infographic Post

structure.guidance: Brief context for the infographic. What information does it contain and why does it matter? 50-75 words.
The infographic image with descriptive alt text containing focus keyword.

structure.heading: Key Highlights from the Infographic
structure.guidance: Text version of the main infographic points — essential for SEO since Google can't read image text. 200-400 words.

structure.heading: Share This Infographic
structure.guidance: Embed code for other bloggers to share. This earns backlinks. 25 words + embed code.
CTA to related content. 25-50 words.

templates.seo_notes: Text content is critical — Google indexes the text, not the image. Include embed code to earn backlinks. Alt text must be descriptive and keyword-rich.

templates.name: Opinion / Thought Leadership

structure.guidance: State your opinion boldly upfront. Don't hedge. Tell the reader exactly what you believe and why they should care. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Why Most People Get This Wrong
structure.guidance: The conventional wisdom you're challenging. Be respectful but direct. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Here's What I Actually Think
structure.guidance: Your position, fully argued with evidence, examples, or personal experience. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: The Evidence That Changed My Mind
structure.guidance: Data, research, or experiences that support your view. Intellectual honesty builds trust. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: What This Means Going Forward
structure.guidance: Implications of your position. What should readers do differently? 150-200 words.
Invite disagreement. Ask readers for their take. Controversial = more comments = more engagement signals. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Bold takes earn more social shares and links than safe takes. The controversy itself can be a traffic driver. Include your byline with credentials — E-E-A-T matters here.

templates.name: Year in Review / Annual Report

structure.guidance: The headline metric or achievement from the year. Set the tone — honest and reflective. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: By the Numbers: {Year} Highlights
structure.guidance: Key metrics: traffic, revenue, subscribers, products launched, posts published. Use a stat box or table. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: What Worked Well
structure.guidance: Your top 3-5 wins with specific results. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: What Didn't Work
structure.guidance: Be honest about failures. Readers appreciate transparency and it's rare — makes you memorable. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Lessons Learned
structure.guidance: Distilled wisdom from both successes and failures. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Plans for {Next Year}
structure.guidance: Goals and experiments planned. Creates accountability. 200-300 words.
Thank your audience. Ask about their year. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Publish between Dec 20 - Jan 10 for maximum reach. 'Year in Review' searches spike massively in this window. Include the year in the title and URL.

templates.name: Resource Page / Link Roundup

structure.guidance: What this resource page covers, who curated it, and how often it's updated. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: Essential {Category} Resources
structure.guidance: Top-tier resources in this category with a brief description of why each is valuable. 300-500 words.

structure.heading: Recommended {Category} Tools
structure.guidance: Tools, software, or platforms. Same format. 200-400 words.

structure.heading: Best {Category} Books
structure.guidance: Books worth reading. Include author and a one-sentence description. 150-300 words.

structure.heading: Courses and Training
structure.guidance: Educational resources. Free and paid. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Communities and Forums
structure.guidance: Where to connect with others in this space. 100-150 words.
How often this page is updated. Invite suggestions. 50 words.

templates.seo_notes: Resource pages are highly linkable — outreach campaigns love them. Email every resource you mention asking for a share. Update quarterly. Target '[topic] resources' keyword.

templates.name: Newsletter Issue / Email Content

structure.guidance: Personal, conversational opener. What's on your mind this week? 50-75 words.

structure.heading: This Week's Main Idea
structure.guidance: One core insight, tip, or story. Focused — don't try to cover everything. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: What I'm Reading/Watching/Using
structure.guidance: 2-3 curated recommendations with brief context for each. 75-150 words.

structure.heading: One Question for You
structure.guidance: A single question to invite replies. Replies improve deliverability and build relationship. 25-50 words.

templates.seo_notes: Newsletters aren't indexed by Google — focus on subscriber value. High-performing newsletters can be repurposed into blog posts for SEO.

templates.name: Podcast Show Notes

structure.guidance: Episode title, guest name (if applicable), 2-3 sentence summary of what's covered. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: What You'll Learn in This Episode
structure.guidance: 3-5 bullet points of key takeaways. Highly skimmable. 75-150 words.

structure.heading: Episode Highlights
structure.guidance: Timestamped key moments. Example: '00:15:30 — How [Guest] grew from 0 to 10,000 subscribers'. 200-400 words.

structure.heading: Resources Mentioned
structure.guidance: Everything mentioned in the episode with links. Very useful for listeners. 100-200 words.

structure.heading: Full Transcript
structure.guidance: Include full or edited transcript. Google indexes transcripts — massive SEO benefit. 500-3000 words.

templates.seo_notes: Transcripts are the most important SEO element of show notes. Target the episode topic as the primary keyword. Include guest's name for branded searches.

templates.name: Video Script / YouTube Description

structure.heading: HOOK (First 15 seconds)
structure.guidance: State the payoff immediately — what will the viewer learn/get. Create a pattern interrupt. Never start with 'Hey guys welcome back'. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: INTRO (15-60 seconds)
structure.guidance: Expand on what's covered and why the viewer should keep watching. Brief credibility statement. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: Main Point 1
structure.guidance: First major section. Script each point fully. Add '(PAUSE FOR B-ROLL)' notes. 300-500 words.

structure.heading: Main Point 2
structure.guidance: Second section. Include an example or demonstration. 300-500 words.

structure.heading: Main Point 3
structure.guidance: Third section. 300-500 words.

structure.heading: OUTRO (Last 30 seconds)
structure.guidance: Summary of key points. Ask for like/subscribe/comment. Preview next video. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: YouTube description: keyword in first 2 lines (above fold), full description 250+ words, tags, chapter markers. Title: primary keyword in first 60 characters.

templates.name: FAQ Page

structure.guidance: Brief intro — what questions this FAQ covers, who it's for. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: General Questions
structure.guidance: 5-8 broad questions about your product/service/topic. Q&A format. 40-60 words per answer.

structure.heading: Pricing and Plans
structure.guidance: 4-6 pricing-related questions. Very important for conversions.

structure.heading: Technical Questions
structure.guidance: 4-6 technical or setup questions.

structure.heading: Account and Billing
structure.guidance: 4-6 account management questions.

structure.heading: Still Have Questions?
structure.guidance: Contact information or support link. 25-50 words.

templates.seo_notes: Apply FAQPage schema to entire page. Target 'X FAQ' and question-format keywords. Source questions from actual customer support tickets and Google PAA.

templates.name: About Page

structure.guidance: Lead with the reader's problem or aspiration — not 'We were founded in...'. Make it about them first. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: Our Story
structure.guidance: How you started, what problem you set out to solve, and why you're uniquely qualified to solve it. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Who We Help
structure.guidance: Specific description of your audience. The more specific, the more the right people feel seen. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Meet the Team
structure.guidance: Photos and brief bios. Human faces dramatically increase trust. 100-200 words.
CTA — what should the visitor do next? 25-50 words.

templates.seo_notes: Apply Organization schema. Include your primary keyword naturally. Link to your most important content pages. About pages are often a top-5 visited page — optimize for conversion.

templates.name: Seasonal / Holiday Content

structure.guidance: Connect the topic to the season or holiday. Establish relevance and urgency. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: Why {Season/Holiday} Matters for {topic}
structure.guidance: Context and relevance. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: {Seasonal Content Section 1}
structure.guidance: Main seasonal content. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: {Seasonal Content Section 2}
structure.guidance: Second section. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: {Seasonal Content Section 3}
structure.guidance: Third section. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 4-5 season-specific FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.
Time-sensitive CTA. 50-75 words.

templates.seo_notes: Publish 6-8 weeks before the season/holiday for maximum ranking time. Use evergreen URLs without the year so the post ranks every year. Update annually.

templates.name: Personal Finance / Money Post

structure.guidance: State the financial outcome readers will achieve. Include your qualifications upfront — YMYL content requires E-E-A-T. 100-150 words.
Standard disclaimer: 'This content is for educational purposes only. Consult a licensed financial advisor before making financial decisions.' Required for YMYL.

structure.heading: Understanding {Financial Topic}
structure.guidance: Clear explanation of the financial concept. No jargon without definition. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: The Numbers: What You Need to Know
structure.guidance: Specific figures, rates, thresholds, or benchmarks. Tables or charts work well here. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Step-by-Step: How to {Financial Action}
structure.guidance: Actionable steps. Very specific. 300-500 words.

structure.heading: Common Mistakes That Cost People Money
structure.guidance: 3-5 costly mistakes to avoid. Highly engaging and shareable. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Real Examples
structure.guidance: Worked examples with numbers. Makes abstract concepts concrete. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5-6 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.
Recap key points. Remind reader to consult a professional for their specific situation. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: YMYL content — E-E-A-T is critical. Include author credentials. Cite authoritative sources (IRS, SEC, official government sites). Review and update whenever tax laws or regulations change.

templates.name: Health and Wellness Post

structure.guidance: State the health topic and what readers will learn. Author credentials required upfront. 100-150 words.
Medical disclaimer: 'This content is for informational purposes only and should not replace professional medical advice. Consult your healthcare provider before making health decisions.'

structure.heading: What the Research Says About {topic}
structure.guidance: Cite peer-reviewed studies. Link to PubMed, NHS, Mayo Clinic, or similar authoritative sources. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Signs and Symptoms to Know
structure.guidance: If applicable. When to seek immediate medical attention. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Evidence-Based Approaches
structure.guidance: What actually works — backed by research. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: What to Avoid
structure.guidance: Common myths debunked. Products or practices to avoid. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: When to See a Doctor
structure.guidance: Clear guidance on when professional help is needed. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5-6 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.
Remind readers to consult healthcare providers. 75 words.

templates.seo_notes: YMYL content — highest E-E-A-T requirements. Medical reviewer credentials must be displayed. Cite studies with PubMed links. Reviewed-by-medical-expert byline dramatically improves rankings for health content.

templates.name: Travel Guide

structure.guidance: Why this destination? Set the scene with vivid, specific details. When you visited and your overall impression. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Quick Facts About {Destination}
structure.guidance: Best time to visit, how to get there, currency, language, timezone, visa requirements. Table format works well.

structure.heading: Where to Stay in {Destination}
structure.guidance: 3-4 accommodation recommendations across budget levels. Include neighborhoods to stay in. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: Top Things to Do in {Destination}
structure.guidance: 8-12 activities or attractions with practical details (address, hours, cost). 500-700 words.

structure.heading: Where to Eat in {Destination}
structure.guidance: Restaurant recommendations by meal type or neighborhood. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: Getting Around {Destination}
structure.guidance: Transport options, costs, apps to download. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: {Destination} Travel Tips
structure.guidance: Insider tips from your experience. Safety, etiquette, money-saving hacks. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Sample {duration} Itinerary
structure.guidance: Day-by-day schedule. Very practical and highly shareable. 300-500 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5-6 FAQs about visiting. Apply FAQPage schema.
Final recommendation. Invite readers to share their tips. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Target '{destination} travel guide {year}', 'things to do in {destination}', '{destination} itinerary'. Add TouristAttraction schema for key sites mentioned. Update annually — tourism info changes.

templates.name: Recipe Post

structure.guidance: A brief personal story or context for the recipe. Why you love it. What makes this version special. 75-150 words. (Don't write too much before the recipe — readers hate scrolling.)

structure.heading: Why You'll Love This Recipe
structure.guidance: 3-5 bullet points: quick, easy, kid-friendly, etc. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: Ingredients
structure.guidance: Full ingredient list. Include weights not just cups. Note substitutions for dietary restrictions. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Step-by-Step Instructions
structure.guidance: Numbered steps. Each step = one action. Include temperatures and timing. Photos at key stages. 200-400 words.

structure.heading: Tips and Variations
structure.guidance: Pro tips for best results. Common variations (vegan, gluten-free, etc.). Storage instructions. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 4-5 recipe-specific FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.

templates.seo_notes: Apply full Recipe schema (prepTime, cookTime, calories, yield, ingredients). This unlocks rich results with recipe card in Google. Recipe title should be the keyword. Include high-quality food photography.

templates.name: Software / App Tutorial

structure.guidance: What software/app is being covered, what the reader will achieve, version number covered. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: System Requirements and Setup
structure.guidance: Minimum requirements, how to download/install, initial setup. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Getting Started: The Interface Overview
structure.guidance: Key areas of the UI labeled with a screenshot. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Step 1: [First Key Task]
structure.guidance: The most common or first task users need to complete. Screenshot each step. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Step 2: [Second Key Task]
structure.guidance: Second task. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Step 3: [Third Key Task]
structure.guidance: Third task. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Tips and Shortcuts
structure.guidance: Power user tips, keyboard shortcuts, hidden features. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Troubleshooting Common Issues
structure.guidance: 3-5 issues users commonly encounter with solutions. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 4-5 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.

templates.seo_notes: Include software version in title (e.g., 'Photoshop 2026'). Screenshots must show the exact current UI. Update when software gets major updates — outdated tutorials rank poorly.

templates.name: Template / Framework Reveal

structure.guidance: What problem this template/framework solves. The result you achieved using it. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: The Complete Template
structure.guidance: The actual template in full. Use a styled box or code block. This is what readers came for — don't hide it.

structure.heading: How to Use This Template
structure.guidance: Step-by-step guide to filling it in or applying it. 300-400 words.

structure.heading: Why This Template Works
structure.guidance: The psychology or logic behind why each element is structured the way it is. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Real Examples
structure.guidance: 2-3 filled-in examples showing it in action. 200-350 words.

structure.heading: Variations for Different Use Cases
structure.guidance: How to adapt the template for different situations. 150-200 words.
How to get the downloadable version (lead magnet opportunity). 50-75 words.

templates.seo_notes: Title: '[Topic] Template (Free Download)' or 'The [Name] Framework'. Template posts earn 3x more links than average blog posts. Gate the downloadable version for email capture.

templates.name: Prediction / Forecast Post

structure.guidance: Why predictions matter now. Your qualifications to make them. Brief preview of top predictions. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: State of {Industry} in {Current Year}
structure.guidance: Where things stand right now — the baseline. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Prediction 1: [Specific Prediction]
structure.guidance: State the prediction boldly. Evidence supporting it. Confidence level (high/medium/low). Impact if true. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: What to Do to Prepare
structure.guidance: Actionable advice based on these predictions. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: My Track Record
structure.guidance: If you've made predictions before — how did you do? Honesty builds credibility. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Publish in Q4 or Q1 when '[year] [industry] predictions' searches surge. Bold predictions get more links and shares than hedged ones. Update with results at year end.

templates.name: Email Outreach / Cold Email Guide

structure.guidance: The problem with most cold emails. Your results using the approach you're about to share. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Why Most Cold Emails Fail
structure.guidance: Common mistakes. What recipients actually want. 200-250 words.

structure.heading: The Anatomy of a Perfect Cold Email
structure.guidance: Break down each element: subject line, opener, value prop, CTA. 250-350 words.

structure.heading: Subject Lines That Get Opened
structure.guidance: 10+ proven subject line formulas with examples. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: {Number} Cold Email Templates That Work
structure.guidance: Full email templates for different scenarios. The more templates, the more linkable. 400-600 words.

structure.heading: The Follow-Up Sequence
structure.guidance: How many follow-ups, timing, what to say. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: How to Personalize at Scale
structure.guidance: Tools and techniques for mass personalization. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Measuring Success: Key Metrics
structure.guidance: Open rate, reply rate, conversion rate benchmarks. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.

templates.seo_notes: Templates are the most shared element — make them prominent. Target 'cold email template' and '[use case] outreach email' keywords.

templates.name: Affiliate / Commission Content

structure.guidance: FTC-required affiliate disclosure at the very top: 'This post contains affiliate links. If you purchase through my links, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.'
Your experience with the product category. Why you're qualified to review it. Bottom-line recommendation upfront. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Quick Picks
structure.guidance: Top 3 recommendations for different buyer types. High skimmability.

structure.heading: How I Tested These Products
structure.guidance: Your evaluation process and criteria. Builds credibility for recommendations. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Full Reviews
structure.guidance: Individual reviews of each product. Features, pros, cons, pricing, verdict. 200-350 words each.

structure.heading: Buying Guide: What to Look For
structure.guidance: Decision criteria for a buyer in this category. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5-6 buyer FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.

structure.heading: Our Top Recommendation
structure.guidance: Final verdict with clear CTA. 100-150 words.

templates.seo_notes: FTC disclosure is legally required. Target 'best [product category]' and '[product] review' keywords. Include real photos — not just press kit images. Update when products are discontinued or replaced.

templates.name: SaaS Landing Page

structure.guidance: Headline: The specific transformation your software creates. Subheadline: Who it's for and how it works in one sentence. CTA button above the fold.

structure.heading: The Problem
structure.guidance: Agitate the pain your software solves. Specific and emotional. 75-150 words.

structure.heading: How {Product} Works
structure.guidance: 3-step simple process. Keep it simple: 1. Do X → 2. Do Y → 3. Get Z. 75-150 words.

structure.heading: Key Features
structure.guidance: 3-6 features written as benefits. Icon + headline + 2 sentences each.

structure.heading: Social Proof
structure.guidance: 3-5 customer testimonials with specific results. Include photos and company names.

structure.heading: Pricing
structure.guidance: Clear pricing tiers. Highlight the recommended plan. Annual discount clearly shown.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 6-8 conversion-focused FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema. Address the most common objections.
Final CTA with risk reversal (free trial, money-back guarantee). 50-75 words.

templates.seo_notes: Target your primary keyword in H1. Apply SoftwareApplication schema. Landing pages need fewer links and more conversion focus — don't link out to competitors.

templates.name: Pillar Page for Topic Cluster

structure.guidance: Broad overview of the topic. Why it matters. Table of contents with links to all sections. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: What Is {Broad Topic}?
structure.guidance: Clear definition targeting 'what is' search queries. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: {Sub-Topic 1} [Link to cluster post]
structure.guidance: 300-400 word overview of this subtopic. Link to the dedicated cluster post for full coverage.

structure.heading: {Sub-Topic 2} [Link to cluster post]
structure.guidance: 300-400 word overview. Link to cluster post.

structure.heading: {Sub-Topic 3} [Link to cluster post]
structure.guidance: 300-400 word overview. Link to cluster post.

structure.heading: {Sub-Topic 4} [Link to cluster post]
structure.guidance: 300-400 word overview. Link to cluster post.

structure.heading: {Sub-Topic 5} [Link to cluster post]
structure.guidance: 300-400 word overview. Link to cluster post.

structure.heading: Getting Started with {Broad Topic}
structure.guidance: Actionable first steps. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 6-8 FAQs covering the full breadth. Apply FAQPage schema.
Next steps. Point to the most relevant cluster posts based on reader goal. 100-150 words.

templates.seo_notes: This page links TO all cluster posts. All cluster posts link BACK to this page. Target broad 1-2 word head keyword. Update whenever a new cluster post is published.

templates.name: Myth-Busting Post

structure.guidance: Why myths about this topic are dangerous or costly. How many myths will be debunked. Your qualification to assess them. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Myth 1: [Common False Belief]
structure.guidance: State the myth. Explain why people believe it. Present the evidence against it. The truth. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Where These Myths Come From
structure.guidance: Why misinformation spreads in this field. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: The Bottom Line
structure.guidance: Summary of what's actually true. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Highly linkable and shareable. Target '[topic] myths' keyword. The more authoritative your myth-busting evidence, the more links you'll attract.

templates.name: Salary / Pricing Guide

structure.guidance: Why this data matters and how it was collected. Date of data collection. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: {Topic} Salary / Pricing Overview
structure.guidance: High-level averages with a summary table. The most-searched data points up front. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: By Experience Level
structure.guidance: Entry, mid, senior breakdowns. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: By Location
structure.guidance: Top cities or regions compared. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: By Industry or Niche
structure.guidance: How different industries affect rates. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Factors That Affect {Salary/Price}
structure.guidance: What drives numbers up or down. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: How to Negotiate
structure.guidance: Practical negotiation advice. Very high engagement section. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5-6 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.

templates.seo_notes: Very high-intent searches. Update annually — stale salary data destroys credibility. Include the year prominently in title and URL. Target '[role] salary {year}' keywords.

templates.name: Best Practices Post

structure.guidance: Why best practices matter for this topic. What following them achieves. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: Best Practice 1: [Specific Practice]
structure.guidance: What it is, why it matters, and how to implement it. 200-300 words each.

structure.heading: Common Violations to Avoid
structure.guidance: What NOT to do — the flip side of best practices. 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 4-5 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.
Prioritization advice — if the reader can only do 3 things from this list, which 3? 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Target '[topic] best practices {year}'. Very evergreen content. Update annually. Great for establishing topical authority.

templates.name: Interview Prep Guide

structure.guidance: What this guide covers, what type of interview, success rate context. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: What to Expect
structure.guidance: Interview format, stages, typical timeline. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: How to Prepare (2-Week Plan)
structure.guidance: Day-by-day or week-by-week prep schedule. Very actionable. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Common Interview Questions (With Answers)
structure.guidance: 15-25 questions with sample answers. This is what people came for. 600-1000 words.

structure.heading: Questions to Ask the Interviewer
structure.guidance: 10-15 smart questions to ask at the end. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: What to Do After the Interview
structure.guidance: Follow-up email template, timeline expectations. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Red Flags to Watch For
structure.guidance: Signs the company or role isn't right. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 5-6 FAQs. Apply FAQPage schema.

templates.seo_notes: Very high intent — people searching this are actively job hunting. Target '[role] interview questions'. Include the actual Q&As as they are what earn the featured snippets.

templates.name: Content Upgrade / Lead Magnet Landing Page

structure.guidance: Headline: The specific thing they're getting. Sub-headline: The specific benefit. Opt-in form above fold.

structure.heading: What's Inside
structure.guidance: Bullet list of exactly what's included. Specific > vague. 50-100 words.

structure.heading: Who This Is For
structure.guidance: 2-3 specific reader types this is designed for. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: Privacy Note
structure.guidance: One-line privacy reassurance: 'We never spam. Unsubscribe anytime.' Required for trust.

templates.seo_notes: These pages are conversion-optimized, not SEO-optimized. Minimal text, minimal links. Focus on the single action: email opt-in.

templates.name: Roundup of Industry News

structure.guidance: The week/month in one sentence. The single biggest story. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: The Big Story: [Headline]
structure.guidance: The most important news item in full context. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Also in the News
structure.guidance: 4-6 shorter news items with brief commentary. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: What to Watch Next Week
structure.guidance: Upcoming events, announcements, or trends to monitor. 75-100 words.
Ask readers what they're watching. 25-50 words.

templates.seo_notes: Consistent publishing schedule builds returning audience. Target '[industry] news [week/month year]'. These posts compound — readers bookmark and return.

templates.name: Course / Training Program Overview

structure.guidance: What the student will be able to DO after completing this course. Specific outcome. CTA above fold.

structure.heading: What You'll Learn
structure.guidance: Module-by-module breakdown. Specific skills and outcomes per module. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: Who This Course Is For
structure.guidance: Ideal student profile. Also who it's NOT for — reduces refunds. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: What's Included
structure.guidance: Videos, downloads, community access, coaching calls, lifetime access. 75-150 words.

structure.heading: Student Results
structure.guidance: 3-5 testimonials with specific outcomes. 'I went from X to Y' format. 150-200 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 8-10 pre-purchase FAQs. Address every objection. Apply FAQPage schema.
Final CTA with urgency element and risk reversal (money-back guarantee). 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Apply Course schema. Target '[topic] course' and '[topic] training' keywords. Student testimonials with specific results are your strongest conversion element.

templates.name: Retrospective / Lessons Learned

structure.guidance: What is being reviewed (project, year, campaign). Time period. Your honest overall assessment. 75-100 words.

structure.heading: What We Set Out to Do
structure.guidance: Original goals and expectations. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: What Actually Happened
structure.guidance: Honest account of the reality vs expectations. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: The Wins
structure.guidance: What genuinely went well and why. Be specific. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: The Failures
structure.guidance: What didn't work. The more honest, the more trust you build. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: The Lessons
structure.guidance: What you'd do differently. Distilled wisdom. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: What's Next
structure.guidance: How these lessons will be applied going forward. 75-100 words.

templates.seo_notes: Authenticity and transparency are the engagement drivers here. Readers appreciate honesty about failures. First-person account builds E-E-A-T.

templates.name: Job Description / Hiring Post

structure.guidance: Role title, company culture in 2-3 sentences. Why this is a great opportunity. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: What You'll Do
structure.guidance: 5-8 specific responsibilities. Use action verbs. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: What We're Looking For
structure.guidance: Must-have requirements (short list). Nice-to-have skills (separate list). 100-150 words.

structure.heading: What We Offer
structure.guidance: Salary range, benefits, remote policy, growth opportunities. 75-150 words.

structure.heading: How to Apply
structure.guidance: Clear application instructions. Deadline if applicable. 50-75 words.

templates.seo_notes: Apply JobPosting schema with salary range (required by Google for Jobs eligibility). Target '[role title] job' keywords. Include salary — job posts with salary listed get 75% more applications.

templates.name: Agency Service Page

structure.guidance: Service name + the outcome it delivers. Who you serve. Single CTA. 50-75 words.

structure.heading: The Problem We Solve
structure.guidance: Paint the pain without the service. Be specific to your ideal client's situation. 100-150 words.

structure.heading: Our {Service} Process
structure.guidance: 3-5 step process with clear descriptions of what happens at each stage. 200-300 words.

structure.heading: What's Included
structure.guidance: Specific deliverables. Clients want to know exactly what they're paying for. 100-200 words.

structure.heading: Client Results
structure.guidance: 3-5 case study snippets with specific outcomes (traffic %, revenue, rankings). 150-250 words.

structure.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
structure.guidance: 6-8 service-specific FAQs. Address pricing objections. Apply FAQPage schema.
Clear next step CTA. Free consultation, audit, or quote. 50-75 words.

templates.seo_notes: Apply Service schema or LocalBusiness schema. Target '[service type] agency' and '[service] services'. Include specific results — vague promises don't rank or convert.
